statusText: Mapped policy state: WATCH. Cash NDX is at 30,279.00 after printing a 30,264.51 session low: the 64-point bounce off that low has faded and the index is back within 15 points of it, which is a failed retracement close to a session extreme. The 10-year is at a 5.27% session high and the 30-year at 5.59%, the highest since 2004. Total cash range is still only 0.55% and VIX is 16.09, so Tail sits at the top of the watch band rather than in the elevated band.
recommendation: Tail remains below the block threshold, so the mapped state is WATCH for both NQ futures and the NAS100 CFD. No danger window is flagged for the remainder of the September 29 US session, which has no further scheduled high-impact release. The flagged window covers 12:00 to 15:00 UTC on September 30, spanning the 12:15 UTC ADP employment change, the 12:30 UTC block of August core PCE, personal spending, the third estimate of Q2 GDP and the advance goods trade balance, the delayed second leg into the 13:30 UTC cash open and 13:45 UTC Chicago PMI, and the post-open hour containing the 14:30 UTC EIA crude stocks change; the published forecast maps those three hours to BLOCK_NEW_BASE_ENTRIES. Outside that window the forecast holds the watch band and reaches the low band through the US evening and Asian overnight hours. Existing-position management and emergency protection are unaffected by this mapping.
headline: Cash NDX retests its 30,264.51 session low as a 64-point bounce fades, with the 10-year at a 5.27% session high and the 30-year at 5.59%, its highest since 2004; the 0.55% range and a 16.09 VIX keep Tail at the watch-band top
body: The clearest current evidence is the cash Nasdaq-100. It opened at 30,412.29, made an early 30,429.97 high, fell through its 30,276.81 prior close to a 30,264.51 session low after the 14:00 UTC data block, bounced roughly 64 points to 30,328.75 around 15:02 UTC, and has since given that bounce back almost entirely to trade 30,279.00, down 7.56 points or 0.02% and about 15 points above the low. A cross-check on the QQQ tracking fund at 15:34 UTC agrees, at 737.58 inside a 736.26 to 740.58 range against a 736.53 prior close. That sequence is a failed retracement with the index close to its session extreme, which is a genuine Tail amplifier and the reason Tail rises from 20 an hour earlier to the top of the watch band. Three things keep it out of the elevated band. The total cash range is 165.46 points, or 0.55%, so there is no meaningful directional displacement to extend. NQ front-month futures still trade 30,629.25, up 63.00 points or 0.21% against a 30,566.25 prior close, having covered 30,372.25 to 30,725.50 and visited both extremes with retracements. And implied volatility has not confirmed: VIX trades 16.09, up 0.02 points or 0.12%, inside a 15.73 to 16.19 range. The genuine amplifier is duration. The ten-year trades 5.27%, up three basis points from a 5.24% prior close and at its session high, while the thirty-year has reached 5.59%, reported today as the highest since 2004; the Federal Reserve H.15 release for September 25 had the two-year at 4.81%, the ten-year at 5.17% and the thirty-year at 5.49%, so roughly ten basis points of the move is fresh. CME FedWatch has been cited near a 70% probability of an October hike. Today's data was weak but was absorbed: Conference Board consumer confidence fell to 81.9 against an 89.2 consensus and an 88.6 prior, its lowest since 2014, August JOLTS job openings printed 7.079 million against a 7.23 million consensus, and the Dallas Fed services index came in at -1.8, while Case-Shiller home prices rose 2.5% year over year and the FHFA house price index 2.6%. University of Michigan sentiment at 48.1 for September corroborates the weak consumer signal. Crude has eased, with WTI down 1.13% to 91.55 and Brent down 0.80% to 104.44 as United States and Iran mediation continues, removing one of Monday's pressures. The shared Finviz context file was collected at 14:22 UTC, inside the 90-minute freshness limit, and was used only as supporting cross-asset context: its collection status is partial with the futures and calendar sections unavailable, and its breadth, megacap and semiconductor sections are explicitly labelled latest-session and non-real-time, so they cannot establish current NQ structure. Those sections show internal divergence, with all seven tracked semiconductors positive at a mean change near 1.9% against only three of eight megacaps positive and Apple and Alphabet lower. That conflict reduces directional conviction and supports elevated Stress rather than Tail. Its earnings section flags Micron after tomorrow's close, verified as a September 30 event rather than today's. All price, yield, volatility, oil and release evidence above comes from independent current research, and every headline taken from the Finviz feed was treated as discovery only. Tomorrow's 12:30 UTC timing for August personal income and outlays and the third estimate of Q2 GDP was confirmed against the Bureau of Economic Analysis release schedule. The net picture is high but slowly decaying Stress, one live duration amplifier, one failed retracement at a session low, and no persistent one-way structure of any size, which places Tail at 24.

lookbackSummary: 23 of the 24 preceding hours were published; the 14:00 UTC slot is unavailable because no Claude assessment was published in that clock hour. Tail ranged from 17 to 24 across the available hours and never reached the elevated band. Tail troughed at 17 through the late Monday and early Tuesday overnight session, printed 24 at 01:00, 03:00 and 04:00 UTC during the European handover as the duration selloff was repriced, then held 20 to 21 in each of the last nine available hours. Stress declined steadily from 84 to 74 as implied volatility decayed from Monday's selloff. Confidence held between 86 and 88 throughout. The dominant mode was mixed for 14 hours, normal for 4 hours, trend-down for 4 hours and trend-up for 1 hour.
outlookSummary: The published forecast keeps Tail at the top of the watch band for the current hour, where a failed retracement at the cash session low is actually observed, then eases through the September 29 afternoon lull and into the low band across the US evening and Asian overnight window, which is the pattern the lookback recorded a day earlier. Tail returns to the watch band from the Asian afternoon onward and builds gradually as positioning for the September 30 release block develops. The horizon contains one elevated-band window of 3 hours, from 12:00 to 14:00 UTC on September 30: the 12:15 UTC ADP employment change and the 12:30 UTC block of August core PCE, personal spending, the third estimate of Q2 GDP and the advance goods trade balance; the delayed second leg into the 13:30 UTC cash open and the 13:45 UTC Chicago PMI, where conditional Tail peaks at 28; and the post-open hour containing the 14:30 UTC EIA crude stocks change. Stress is forecast to decay from 76 to 69 overnight before rebuilding to 79 into the release block, and Confidence steps down from 88 to 74 across the horizon as the current price-path evidence ages. Every hour beyond the current clock hour describes a conditional path rather than observed structure.

A failed retracement at a session extreme with duration aligned holds Tail at the top of the watch band.

The assumption is that no new duration impulse arrives; a fresh move above the 5.27% session high in the 10-year would invalidate that easing.

drivers: Scenario: late-session imbalance converting drift into a one-way close
Conditional on where the cash index sits relative to its session low

drivers: Closing auction is the hour's main conditional amplifier

No US single-name catalyst scheduled in this hour
